title: SEC-TESTS: bt5.11 HLC overflow test uses internal struct access
description: The HLC overflow regression tests (hlc.rs send_logical_overflow_advances_wall and receive_logical_overflow_advances_wall) construct HlcClock directly by accessing the 'last' and 'node_id' private fields: HlcClock { last: HlcTimestamp { wall_ms: 1000, logical: u32::MAX, node_id: NODE_A }, node_id: NODE_A }. This is only possible because the struct fields are pub within the module (cfg(test) struct literal). If HlcClock fields are ever made truly private (not pub), these tests will not compile. More importantly, seeding the clock at u32::MAX logical is the only way to trigger the overflow path — this is correct and necessary. The oracle for these tests is derived from the HLC algorithm (Kulkarni & Demirbas 2014): send() at (wall=1000, logical=u32::MAX) must produce (wall=1001, logical=0), and the result must be strictly greater than the seed. This is adequate. No issue with the oracle — filing this as informational: the test depends on non-private field access and would break if fields were encapsulated. Not a test integrity violation, but a fragility worth tracking.
